startLearning.title: How to start learning piano online
startLearning.excerpt: You do not need a real piano to begin. Here is a simple plan for your first weeks.

content.text: Starting piano can feel intimidating, but the first steps are small. With a virtual piano in your browser you can build finger familiarity, ear training and rhythm before you ever buy an instrument.

The keyboard repeats the same pattern of white and black keys. Black keys come in groups of two and three, and the white key just before a group of two is always C. Once you can find C, you can find every other note.

items: Ten to fifteen focused minutes beat one long session per week.
Start with one hand, slowly, and only add speed when it feels easy.
Say the note names out loud as you play them.
Finish each session with something you enjoy, even if it is simple.

content.text: Recording a short phrase and listening back is one of the fastest ways to notice uneven rhythm or wrong notes. It also lets you track your progress over the weeks.

choosingKeys.title: 25, 49, 61 or 88 keys? Choosing the right piano size
choosingKeys.excerpt: More keys are not always better. Here is how to pick a size that fits your music.

content.text: A full piano has 88 keys, spanning seven octaves plus a few extra notes, from A0 to C8. Smaller keyboards simply cut off the lowest and highest octaves.
What each size is good for

items: 25 and 37 keys: quick melodies and simple ideas, easiest on small screens.
49 keys: a comfortable all-round choice for beginners and for most pop and film melodies.
61 keys: five octaves, enough for many songs with both hands.
76 and 88 keys: needed for a lot of classical repertoire that uses the extreme low and high notes.

content.text: Look at the lowest and highest notes in the pieces you want to play. If they fit in five octaves, a 61-key layout is plenty. If you are not sure, the piano finder on the home page can suggest a size from your goals and level.

customShortcuts.title: Make your computer keyboard feel like a piano
customShortcuts.excerpt: Custom shortcuts help you play faster and more comfortably. Here is how to set them up.

content.text: Playing with the computer keyboard is fast, but only if the layout feels natural to your hands. That is why every note in Web Piano can be mapped to any key you like.

items: Open Settings and find the octave you want to change.
Click the field next to a note, then press the key you want to use.
If a key is already taken, clear the other shortcut first.
Use Reset to defaults any time you want a fresh start.

content.text: Keep white notes on one row and the matching black notes on the row above, like a real keyboard. Group each octave under neighbouring keys so your fingers move in a predictable pattern.

earTraining.title: Five-minute ear training exercises you can do anywhere
earTraining.excerpt: Training your ear makes everything else easier. These short drills fit into any break.

content.text: Ear training means learning to recognize notes, intervals and chords by sound. It speeds up learning songs and makes improvising more natural.

items: Hum then play: sing a note, then find it on the piano.
Up or down: play two notes and decide whether the second is higher or lower, then check.
Copy a melody: pick a tune you know and find it by ear, one note at a time.

content.text: Five minutes a day is enough. Keep the drills light and playful, and you will notice progress within a few weeks.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Quick answers to the things people ask most.

install.question: Do I need to install anything or create an account?
install.answer: No. Web Piano runs entirely in your browser, so you can open the Virtual Piano page and start playing right away. An account is optional and is only needed for your profile page.

loadSounds.question: Why do I have to press “Load piano” first?
loadSounds.answer: The piano uses recorded grand piano samples. They are downloaded once when you press Load piano, so the page opens fast and nothing is fetched until you want to play. After they finish loading, every note plays instantly.

play.question: How can I play the piano?
play.answer: You can click the keys with your mouse, drag across them for a glissando, tap them on a touch screen, use your computer keyboard, or connect a MIDI keyboard. Each computer key is mapped to a piano note.

shortcuts.question: Can I change which computer key plays which note?
shortcuts.answer: Yes. Open Settings, click the field next to any note, and press the key you want. Keys are matched by position, so shortcuts work with any keyboard language, and the app warns you if a key is already used. Your choices are saved in this browser, and you can reset everything to the defaults.

size.question: Which piano size should I choose?
size.answer: Web Piano offers 25, 37, 49, 61, 76 and 88 keys, and 49 keys is the default. If you are just starting out, 49 or 61 keys is a comfortable choice. Use the piano finder on this page if you want a recommendation based on your goals and level.

record.question: Can I record what I play?
record.answer: Yes. On the Virtual Piano page, press record, play your piece, then stop. You can listen to the recording again, download it as an audio file, or clear it and start over.

midi.question: Can I play with a MIDI keyboard?
midi.answer: Yes. Open Settings, press Connect MIDI and allow access in your browser. Notes are played with their real velocity, and you can choose which device to listen to. Web MIDI works in Chrome and Edge, on HTTPS or localhost.

noSound.question: Why is there no sound when I press a key?
noSound.answer: First make sure you pressed Load piano and the sounds have finished loading. Then check that your device is not muted and that the in-app volume is above zero and not muted. If loading failed, press Retry loading.

mobile.question: Does it work on my phone or tablet?
mobile.answer: Yes. Touch is supported, so you can tap and slide across the keys. On a phone, rotating to landscape or choosing a smaller piano size makes the keys easier to hit.
